item.title: Senate Panel Holds Fauci in Contempt of Congress
item.author: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
item.content:encoded: Dr. Anthony Fauci had refused to answer questions at a hearing last week, invoking the Fifth Amendment. Republicans argued that he wasn’t entitled to that protection because he had a presidential pardon.

item.title: Senate Panel Votes to Hold Fauci in Contempt
item.author: Jan Hoffman
item.content:encoded: The case is unique, legal scholars say, because of the tension between the Fifth Amendment and the reach of a presidential pardon. The potential consequences could be grave.

item.title: Trump Made Calls to Warsh in Latest Sign of Bid to Influence Fed
item.author: Josh Wingrove and Enda Curran
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has periodically spoken by phone with Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh since he took the role, people familiar with the matter said, the latest sign of Trump’s effort to exert greater influence over the central bank.

item.title: Lithuania Sees Russia Mulling False-Flag Drone Attack on Region
item.author: Milda Seputyte
item.content:encoded: Lithuania said Russia is weighing a potential false flag operation using captured Ukrainian drones to strike critical infrastructure in the Baltic region.

item.title: US Says Oklo’s Small Nuclear Reactor Reaches ‘Criticality’
item.author: Ari Natter
item.content:encoded: Oklo Inc.’s small modular reactor has reached a key milestone, the Energy Department announced Thursday.

item.title: El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate Primary Win Sets Up the Left’s Biggest Test of the Fall
item.author: Lisa Lerer
item.content:encoded: Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate candidacy poses a critical challenge for Democrats’ ascendant progressive wing: Can an insurgent candidate, with unabashedly liberal positions, win a general election in a moderate state?

item.title: Xi Flexes Expanding Legal Arsenal to Warn Trump Ahead of Summit
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: China’s latest barrage of countermeasures against the US drew on an expanding legal arsenal, demonstrating Beijing’s growing capacity to retaliate while warning Washington against further tech curbs before Xi Jinping’s expected visit next month.

item.title: Virginia Governor to Intervene in NextEra-Dominion Merger
item.author: Emily Forgash
item.content:encoded: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger said she’ll intervene in her state’s review of NextEra Energy Inc.’s $67 billion acquisition of Dominion Energy Inc. over concerns about the deal’s impact of electricity affordability.

item.title: Iceland’s Pro and Anti-EU Camps Tie in Poll Ahead of Referendum
item.author: Ragnhildur Sigurdardottir
item.content:encoded: Iceland is set for a close result in a referendum on resuming talks with the European Union later this month, according to the latest poll.

item.title: Democrats Enter Fundraising Blitz While Bashing Corporate Cash
item.author: Kate Ackley
item.content:encoded: The split-screen is likely to continue through November and into the next Congress.

item.title: US Asks Manila to Extradite Duterte-Allied Pastor Quiboloy Wanted by FBI
item.author: Cliff Venzon
item.content:encoded: The US has asked the Philippines to extradite a Filipino evangelical preacher wanted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation for alleged sex trafficking, risking further political tensions in the Southeast Asian nation.

item.title: India’s Student Movement Shuns Politics, Stays Pressure Group
item.author: Akriti Sharma
item.content:encoded: The Cockroach Janta Party, which spearheaded India’s biggest student protests in recent years, said it won’t become a political party, opting instead to remain a “pressure group” after weeks of demonstrations forced Prime Minister Narendra Modi to replace his education minister.

item.title: Ceuta and Michigan Expose Political Fault Lines Playing Out in Germany
item.author: Alan Crawford
item.content:encoded: Polls for three German state elections next month show the tussle between progressive politics and anti-migrant sentiment.

item.title: Iran Says Deal With Oman on Hormuz Agreed in Principle
item.author: Eltaf Najafizada
item.content:encoded: The wait for an Iran-Oman deal that partially reopens the Strait of Hormuz continued into Thursday, after the Islamic Republic said an agreement on proposed shipping lanes was in the final stages.

item.title: Tennessee’s Andy Ogles Faces Well-Funded Opposition in House Primary Thursday
item.author: Patricia Mazzei, Tim Balk and Emily Cochrane
item.content:encoded: Representative Andy Ogles received President Trump’s endorsement, but his challenger, Charlie Hatcher, a former state agriculture commissioner, has the backing of Gov. Bill Lee.

item.title: Sheinbaum’s Approval Jumps as Inflation Cools to Five-Year Low
item.author: Gonzalo Soto
item.content:encoded: Mexico President Claudia Sheinbaum’s approval rating jumped in July as inflation slowed and economic expectations improved.

item.title: Ukraine Says It Hit Two of Russia’s Oil Refineries Overnight
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Ukraine struck two of Russia’s oil refineries overnight, the latest in a flurry of attacks that signal a resumption of the assault on the nation’s fuel-producing industry.

item.title: North Korea Fires Missile After Warning of Military Steps
item.author: Soo-Hyang Choi
item.content:encoded: North Korea fired a short-range ballistic missile off its east coast Thursday, South Korea’s military said, a day after Pyongyang warned of fresh military steps over Japan’s expanding defense capabilities.

item.title: Commerzbank Says Teaming Up With UniCredit Could Be Positive | Daybreak Europe 8/6/2026
item.content:encoded:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead.
On today's show, Commerzbank says a strategy developed together with UniCredit could be beneficial for investors, extending an olive branch to the Italian rival that’s set to take control of it. The comments came as the German lender announced a €1.2 billion share buyback, after second quarter net income beat estimates.
Siemens has raised its earnings expectations for a second time this year on a surge in data center spending and higher returns from selling software to industry.
Global stocks slipped from record highs, as disappointing guidance from US memory makers Sandisk and Western Digital weighed on sentiment.
And Iran says it has reached an agreement with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.
Today's guest: Bettina Orlopp, Commerzbank CEO & Roland Busch, Siemens CEO (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Denies US Munitions Shortage, Warns ‘Leakers’ of Jail Time
item.author: Ryan Chua
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump denied the US was running low on munitions, saying the country has “massive amounts” of them, while warning of punishment for those who say there’s a shortage.

item.title: Thailand Welcomes Myanmar Leader in Push to End Isolation
item.author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat and Khine Lin Kyaw
item.content:encoded: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul welcomed Myanmar’s former junta chief Min Aung Hlaing on his first visit to Thailand since becoming a civilian leader, underscoring Bangkok’s push to rebuild its neighbor’s ties with other Southeast Asian nations.

item.title: Burnham’s High-Speed Train Dream Hinges on a Fiscal Revolution
item.author: Jacob Reid
item.content:encoded: Mark Haase struggles to draw workers to Crewe.

item.title: Bangladesh ‘Outraged’ With India Over Ex-Leader’s Media Briefing
item.author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen
item.content:encoded: Bangladesh’s government criticized India for allowing former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to conduct a live media briefing from New Delhi, warning that the event undermines efforts to reset bilateral ties between the neighbors.

item.title: F.D.A. Approves Moderna’s mRNA Flu Vaccine
item.author: Christina Jewett
item.content:encoded: The agency had initially refused to even review the application but reversed course after a public outcry.

item.title: José Antonio Kast Kast Unveils Tougher Agenda to Fight Organized Crime
item.author: Antonia Mufarech
item.content:encoded: Chile President José Antonio Kast unveiled a security-focused agenda including a constitutional reform to give the state broader powers to combat crime, seeking to regain momentum on a key pillar of his government.

item.title: C.I.A. Sets Up Secret Cuba Task Force as Trump Pressures Havana
item.author: Adam Entous
item.content:encoded: The task force will allow the spy agency to quickly direct more financial, human and technical resources at the island, with the goal of creating fissures among the Cuban political elite.

item.title: After Michigan Loss, AIPAC Weighs a Second Effort to Defeat El-Sayed
item.author: Jennifer Medina and Theodore Schleifer
item.content:encoded: The pro-Israel organization spent $32 million in an unsuccessful effort to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary. It might try again in the general election.

item.title: Federal Judge Weakens The National Firearms Act
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: The National Firearms Act mandated a permitting process for short-barreled rifles and shotguns, as well as suppressors. A judge ruled that the provision was unconstitutional.

item.title: Mayor Says El-Sayed’s Win Shows He Is More Than a ‘Mini-Mamdani’
item.author: Jeffery C. Mays
item.content:encoded: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York said that Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s close victory in the Michigan Senate primary put “working-class Americans back at the heart of our politics.”

item.title: Trump-Backed Michigan Candidate Loses Primary to Rival Who Suspended His Campaign
item.author: Bayliss Wagner
item.content:encoded: Without running a single ad or filing a campaign finance report, Tom Smith, who had suspended his bid, soundly defeated Amir Hassan, a Navy veteran backed by President Trump.

item.title: Bunny Dolls and Disturbing Allegations: Max Miller’s Strange CNN Interview
item.author: Michael M. Grynbaum
item.content:encoded: In a 23-minute appearance with the anchor Jake Tapper, the Ohio Republican made an unusual effort to rebut a multitude of allegations that have threatened his re-election bid.

item.title: Scandal Leaves North Carolina G.O.P. With No Candidate and Little Time
item.author: Eduardo Medina
item.content:encoded: Representative Chuck Edwards’s decision to drop his re-election bid amid sexual harassment charges came as a Democratic farmer, Jamie Ager, was already making inroads.

item.title: Senate Confirms Dr. Erica Schwartz as C.D.C. Director
item.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
item.content:encoded: Dr. Schwartz, a deputy surgeon general in the first Trump administration, has publicly supported childhood vaccines.

item.title: Why Polling Overestimated Abdul El-Sayed’s Advantage in Michigan
item.author: Ruth Igielnik
item.content:encoded: Surveys greatly overestimated how Dr. Abdul El-Sayed would fare in the state’s Democratic Senate primary, revealing some typical polling challenges.

item.title: U.S. Cuts Ties With Organ Donor Group After Reports of Abuses
item.author: Brian M. Rosenthal
item.content:encoded: The federal government is ending its contract with a Kentucky nonprofit that it says pressured medical workers to remove organs from patients who were getting better.

item.title: Francesca Hong Said Thanksgiving Should Be Canceled. Can Wisconsin Voters Forgive Her?
item.author: Julie Bosman
item.content:encoded: “Cancel Thanksgiving,” she wrote. “VDay” brings out “the worst of humanity,” she mused. Francesca Hong’s old social media posts get a fresh look ahead of Wisconsin’s Democratic primary for governor.

item.title: El-Sayed Got a Big Win for the Left. Can It Win Like This Nationally?
item.author: Nate Cohn
item.content:encoded: The new activist left is built on a coalition that may be too narrow to thrive in Democratic primaries in other areas, particularly the South.

item.title: Cost of Trump’s Namesake Warships Likely to Rise by 50 Percent or More
item.author: John Ismay
item.content:encoded: President Trump’s goal of building a “golden fleet” of 15 battleships could cost $275 billion, according to a government estimate.

item.title: Where El-Sayed Showed Strengths, and Weaknesses, in the Michigan Primary
item.author: Katie Glueck, Caroline Soler and Shane Goldmacher
item.content:encoded: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed had a strong showing in college towns, while Representative Haley Stevens did well in Black urban centers.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed’s Winning New Political Uniform
item.author: Vanessa Friedman
item.content:encoded: Could the black T-shirt and jeans be the next big thing in Washington?

item.title: Why Congress Wants a Closer U.S.-Israel Defense Partnership
item.author: Robert Jimison
item.content:encoded: A proposal making its way through Congress would integrate the U.S. and Israeli defense and intelligence apparatuses more tightly. Some worry that it is a bad idea.

item.title: Suspected Iran Cyberattacks on U.S. Water Supply Follow Years of Warnings and Neglect
item.author: Dustin Volz
item.content:encoded: Federal and state officials are racing to address an assault on the nation’s water supply that they believe is the work of Iranian hackers.

item.title: Abortion Foes Backed Ballot Measures in 2 Red States. Voters Said No.
item.author: Mitch Smith and Ann Hinga Klein
item.content:encoded: Voters in Kansas rejected a proposal to start electing Supreme Court justices, while Missourians declined to make it harder to amend the State Constitution.

item.title: Blanche Defends Pirro but Says Trump Can Fire Her at Any Time
item.author: Devlin Barrett
item.content:encoded: The head of the Justice Department praised the U.S. attorney in Washington after her tense meeting with the president.

item.title: Can Abdul El-Sayed Unify Michigan Democrats Ahead of the General Election?
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: His close margin of victory may point to challenges ahead.

item.title: Trump Seeks a Boost for Hemp That Would Benefit a Top Aide’s Family
item.author: Kenneth P. Vogel, Christina Jewett and Olivia Diaz
item.content:encoded: At the White House’s request, senators tucked a change sought by the hemp industry into a crucial spending bill. It would benefit the son-in-law of Susie Wiles, the president’s chief of staff.

item.title: Muslim Americans Celebrate Abdul El-Sayed’s Win in Michigan Primary
item.author: Madaleine Rubin, Tim Balk, Ama Sarpomaa and Francesca Regalado
item.content:encoded: Muslim voters from across the country said they felt hope and anxiety as Dr. El-Sayed moved closer to becoming the nation’s first Muslim senator.

item.title: Shri Thanedar Is Ousted by a Democratic Socialist in a Michigan House Primary
item.author: Bayliss Wagner
item.content:encoded: Representative Shri Thanedar is among a wave of Democratic incumbents in Congress whom primary voters have sent packing in a surge of anti-incumbent fervor this cycle.

item.title: Takeaways From the Primary Elections in Michigan
item.author: Reid J. Epstein
item.content:encoded: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed narrowly prevailed over Representative Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary for Senate in Michigan, setting up a nervy race to November for the party.
